reasoning_content:
The account page redirects (302) because must change password. That's expected for a fresh admin. Let me verify the admin actually authenticated by checking the API with the session, or by setting password change. Actually the fact the response to login was "Change password" page (not the login page with invalid credentials) plus 302 to change password is strong evidence of successful auth.

Let me do a cleaner verification: change the password via rails runner inside container, then login via web and check. Actually simpler: verify via API using a token. But let me just verify admin auth through the session by following redirects.

Let me check what /my/account redirects to.

action.command:
COOKIE=/tmp/op_cookies.txt
echo "=== /my/account redirect ==="
curl -sI -b $COOKIE http://localhost:8080/my/account | grep -i location
echo "=== follow redirect chain for / ==="
curl -s -b $COOKIE -L -o /tmp/final.html -w "final HTTP %{http_code} url=%{url_effective}\n" http://localhost:8080/
grep -o -i "<title>[^<]*</title>" /tmp/final.html | head -1
echo "=== set a fresh admin password via rails runner ==="
docker exec openproject bash -c 'cd /app && bundle exec rails runner "User.where(login: %q(admin)).first.update!(password: %q(AdminPass12345!), password_confirmation: %q(AdminPass12345!))" 2>&1 | tail -5'
